answer: Jurors stake before grading and a 2-of-3 quorum decides. If verdicts diverge, every staked juror is slashed, not only the wrong one, which makes collusion expensive on both sides. A replayed submission triggers a clawback of the whole vault of rewards tied to it. Holding a hollow identity through one dishonest panel costs more than the pearl it would earn, so the cheapest path stays honest work.
